KERNEL/BaseFeature.h: a hand-written struct, not a standard-library type: every public member is covered, AnnotationState and NamesOfAnnotationState as AnnotationState/NAMES/name, the default, copy/move and map-index constructors as Default/Clone/clone_with_map_index, the Peak2D, RichPeak2D and FeatureHandle constructors as public-field construction, get/setQuality, QualityLess, get/setWidth, get/setCharge and get/setPeptideIdentifications as public fields and field ordering, ==/!= as PartialEq, sortPeptideIdentifications, getAnnotationState as annotation_state, hasPrimaryID/getPrimaryID/clearPrimaryID/setPrimaryID, getIDMatches as the id_matches field, addIDMatch, updateIDReferences.
KERNEL/ChromatogramPeak.h: a hand-written struct, not a standard-library type: every public member is covered, the constructors and assignment as Default/new/Copy, get/setIntensity, get/setRT, get/setPos and get/setPosition as the public rt and intensity fields, ==/!= as PartialEq, IntensityLess, RTLess and PositionLess as scalar comparisons on those fields, operator<< as Display, and the std::hash specialisation as a signed-zero-normalised Hash.
KERNEL/ChromatogramRangeManager.h: a type with no members of its own over the hand-written RangeManager port, not a standard-library type: the class is RangeManager<RangeRT, RangeIntensity, RangeMZ> plus the BaseType alias, which is RangeManager::chromatogram_manager().
KERNEL/ChromatogramTools.h: a hand-written converter, not the standard library: both public members, convertChromatogramsToSpectra and convertSpectraToChromatograms, are convert_chromatograms_to_spectra/convert_spectra_to_chromatograms on MSExperiment, the constructor being trivial.
KERNEL/ConsensusMap.h: a hand-written container, not a standard-library type: docs/MAP_OPERATIONS_SUPPORT.md tables every public member, own and inherited, and maps it (SplitMeta and split, appendRows/appendColumns, ConsensusMap(size_type), setExperimentType, the sort family, swap, findProteinIdentification, the MS run path trio, applyMemberFunction, isMapConsistent as validate_consistency, getUnassignedIDMatches, operator<< as Display; the ExposedVector interface as the public features field). Gaps: getIdentificationData (both overloads) has no counterpart, because the map owns no IdentificationData graph and the caller passes one; the inherited UniqueIdIndexer members updateUniqueIdToIndex, resolveUniqueIdConflicts and swap are not public API (uniqueIdToIndex is unique_id_to_index); the inherited RangeManagerContainer stored range is on-demand ranges(), as for RangeManager.h.
KERNEL/DPeak.h: stays: the header is a compile-time type selector with two specialisations, and Rust code written against the concrete Peak1D and Peak2D needs no metafunction, so the language discharges it with no crate.
KERNEL/Feature.h: a hand-written struct, not a standard-library type: every public member is covered, the constructors as Default/From<BaseFeature>/Clone, get/setOverallQuality as the base quality field, get/setQuality(index) as the named quality_rt/quality_mz fields, OverallQualityLess, get/setConvexHulls and get/setSubordinates as public fields, getConvexHull as convex_hull (recomputed, not cached), encloses, operator== as PartialEq, both applyMemberFunction overloads as for_each_unique_id/count_unique_ids, updateAllIDReferences.

KERNEL/RangeManager.h: a hand-written port, not a standard-library type: MSDim, HasRangeType, RangeBase with every member (constructors, clear, isEmpty, both contains, set/getMin/Max, both extend, extendLeftRight, minSpanIfSingular, clampTo, pushInto, scaleBy, shift, center, getSpan, ==, getNonEmptyRange, operator<<), the RangeRT/RangeMZ/RangeIntensity/RangeMobility accessors as the per-dimension RangeManager methods over an MSDim-tagged RangeBase, and RangeManager's ==, assign(Unsafe), extend(Unsafe), scaleBy, minSpanIfSingular, pushInto(Unsafe), clampTo(Unsafe), both getRangeForDim, hasRange, containsAll, clearRanges, clear(dim) and printRange, with RangeAllType as experiment(). Gap: RangeManagerContainer's stored range has no counterpart; updateRanges/getRange become on-demand range_manager() accessors, so the non-const getRange(), which writes a range into a container that persists until the next updateRanges, cannot be expressed.
